original: First work over $k_0$ and write $H_0=H_{k_0}$. Corestrict $	heta$ to $	heta_0:A	o k_0=\operatorname{Frac}(	heta(A))$; it has the same characteristic as $k$ and every $	heta_0(f_E)$ is nonzero whenever $	heta(f_E)$ is, so [F4] applies and $H_0$ is split. For a simple $M$, take a projective cover $\pi:P\to M$ with superfluous kernel $K$ by [F5]. A nonzero vector of $M$ gives a surjection $H_0\to M$. Projectivity of the free module $H_0$ lifts it to $s:H_0\to P$; the image of $s$ together with $K$ is $P$, so superfluity makes $s$ surjective. Projectivity of $P$ splits $s$, realizing $P$ as a direct summand of $H_0$. Its projection is right multiplication by an idempotent $e$, since a left-linear endomorphism of $H_0$ is determined by its value at $1$. Hence $P\cong H_0e$. Every maximal submodule of $P$ contains $K$: otherwise its sum with $K$ is $P$, contradicting superfluity. Since $K$ itself is maximal, it is the unique maximal submodule, and the head of $P$ is the single copy $M$.
